title: Encapsulate job storage in a JobStore class
description: Brownfield Python refactor: move module-level _jobs dict and _next_id counter into a JobStore class while keeping endpoint behavior identical.

task_spec.prompt:
Refactor src/app.py to encapsulate job state in a JobStore class. All 4 existing tests must still pass.

Add:
  class JobStore:
    def __init__(self) -> None
      — initialises self._jobs: dict[int, str] = {} and self._next_id: int = 1

    def create(self, name: str) -> dict
      — allocates next id, stores status 'pending', returns {id, name, status}

    def get(self, job_id: int) -> dict | None
      — returns {id, status} or None if not found

    def list_all(self) -> list[dict]
      — returns [{id, status}, ...] for all jobs

    def reset(self) -> None
      — clears _jobs and resets _next_id to 1

Replace module-level _jobs / _next_id with:
  _store = JobStore()

Update each endpoint to delegate to _store:
  create_job  -> _store.create(name)
  get_job     -> _store.get(job_id)  (raise 404 if None)
  list_jobs   -> _store.list_all()

Update reset() to call _store.reset().
Do not change endpoint signatures or HTTP semantics.
All 4 existing tests must still pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: JobStore class with __init__, create, get, list_all, reset
get_job delegates to _store.get with 404 on None
success_criteria: uv run python -c "from src.app import app" passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.

check_commands.build: uv run python -c "from src.app import app"
